scene_description: A light-colored classroom or meeting room with rows of long dark-topped tables, white wheeled chairs, a centered two-pane window, patterned walls and two floor lamps on the right.

visible_objects.observations: Both images show tables, white swivel chairs, a two-pane window, two floor lamps, patterned walls and a pale floor. The reference additionally shows a dark vertical element at the far right edge that is not apparent in the candidate.
visible_objects.image_evidence: Reference and candidate, whole frame; reference far right [0.97, 0.46, 1.0, 0.83].

spatial_relations_and_orientation.observations: Both arrange chairs in front of rows of tables, with the window above and lamps at the back right. The candidate compresses the furniture into a narrow horizontal band and gives the room a more symmetrical frontal arrangement; the reference has stronger depth separation and a more prominent right wall.

proportions_and_occlusion.observations: The candidate window and foreground chairs occupy much less image area. Candidate tables and chairs overlap in a flatter, denser strip; in the reference foreground chairs are larger and more separated from the back row. The rightmost chair is cropped in the candidate but contained in the reference.
proportions_and_occlusion.image_evidence: Reference window [0.41, 0.17, 0.60, 0.45], candidate window [0.43, 0.24, 0.57, 0.44]; reference foreground chairs [0.05, 0.52, 0.96, 0.91], candidate [0.09, 0.64, 1.0, 0.88].

materials_and_texture.observations: Both use pale hexagonal wall patterns, pale flooring, dark tabletop surfaces and white chair shells with dark bases. The candidate wall pattern is substantially finer and lower contrast; its table surfaces are lighter and less prominent, and its floor appears more uniformly gray than the reference's subtly mottled pale floor.

visible_geometry.observations: The candidate preserves the window's central divider, rectangular table tops, slender legs and wheeled chair bases. Its chair backs appear smaller and more upright, while the reference foreground chair shells have broader, more conspicuous curved silhouettes. Exact underlying geometry cannot be established from the views.
visible_geometry.image_evidence: Reference window [0.41, 0.17, 0.60, 0.45] and left foreground chair [0.05, 0.52, 0.23, 0.91]; candidate window [0.43, 0.24, 0.57, 0.44] and corresponding left foreground chair [0.09, 0.65, 0.20, 0.88].

camera_and_composition.observations: The reference is closer and oblique, with evident perspective across the tables and a visible right wall corner. The candidate is wider and nearly head-on, showing a ceiling strip, more floor and a smaller central window. These framing differences materially affect the relative sizes and overlap of the furniture.
camera_and_composition.image_evidence: Reference full frame; candidate full frame, especially ceiling [0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.05] and floor [0.0, 0.78, 1.0, 1.0].

lighting_and_shadows.observations: Both are softly lit and have two illuminated floor lamps at right. The reference lamps create distinct warm, bright up-and-down pools on the wall, while the candidate has much weaker, diffuse wall illumination and a cooler, flatter overall appearance.

objects_regions.observation: Reference window is substantially larger in frame than the candidate window at [0.43, 0.24, 0.57, 0.44], although both have two dark-framed panes.
Reference furniture spans more depth and foreground area; candidate furniture [0.05, 0.58, 1.0, 0.88] is compressed into a narrow, almost frontal band.
The reference chair is fully visible; the candidate's rightmost foreground chair at [0.91, 0.64, 1.0, 0.87] is cut off by the frame.
The candidate pattern [0.0, 0.03, 0.42, 0.58] has noticeably smaller, fainter cells.
The two reference lamps produce prominent warm pools of light; candidate lamps at [0.73, 0.34, 0.94, 0.72] produce much subtler illumination.
Partially visible in reference, not apparent in candidate; its identity is uncertain and the different framing may explain its absence.

most_important_visible_defects: Camera and framing differ strongly: candidate is more distant and frontal, changing furniture scale and depth.
Candidate furniture is vertically compressed into a narrow band and the rightmost chair is cropped.
Candidate wall hexagons are finer and fainter, and the lamps lack the reference's strong warm wall light patterns.
uncertainty: Hidden furniture surfaces, exact object counts under occlusion, real-world scale, symmetry and physical contacts cannot be determined reliably from these RGB views. Some apparent size and spacing differences may be caused by camera position or field of view rather than object dimensions.
limitations: Comparison is based only on the two supplied images; the candidate and reference have different framing and perspective. Regions are approximate normalized image coordinates and may identify groups rather than individual objects.
